I checked and legally there's nothing there but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me go through it step by step. First, I was renting a place with this dude, and we were on a lease. When the lease was ending, he just left without giving much notice. He took most of his stuff, leaving only the last bit of his half of the rent and a few things he mentioned in a note he didn't want to bring with him. The place I live in has a rule where if you don't discard your things when you move out, the landlord can pay someone to remove them, and it's a rip-off because they take money from your deposit. I've heard of people losing $250 just for someone to take three milk crates of stuff to the dump. So, I texted and emailed him for two weeks asking him to pick up his things or let me take them to the dump, but he never responded. I ended up taking most of his stuff to the dump, but he had around 60 video games for PS4. I thought, why not sell them? There's a local game store that buys used games, and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Then, last week, I saw him at a party, and we were being polite. He asked how the move-out was, and I said it was good. Naturally, he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games. I told him I tried to get him to grab those things, but he never reached out. Now he's calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked, and legally, there's nothing I can be held responsible for, but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this. Hmm, so the main points are: he left without taking his stuff, I tried to contact him, he didn't respond, I took his stuff to the dump, sold the games, and now he's upset. Legally, I'm in the clear, but is it morally wrong? I think about the effort I put in. I tried to contact him multiple times, gave him a chance to retrieve his stuff. If he didn't respond, maybe it's his loss. But selling his games for $600 seems like a lot. Did I have the right to sell them without his permission? On the other hand, if I had left them, the landlord would have charged him, and he might have lost more money. By selling them, I prevented that loss, but I also made a profit. Is that fair? Or is it taking advantage of his situation? I also consider the emotional aspect. He's upset because he lost his games, and I'm the one who sold them. Even if I tried to contact him, maybe I should have handled it differently, like donating them or leaving them somewhere instead of selling. But legally, I'm fine, so maybe morally, it's a gray area. I did what I thought was best to prevent more loss, but I also made money off his stuff without his consent. That might be why he's upset. I wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I should offer him some of the money back, even though I'm not legally required to. It might help mend the relationship and show that I understand his feelings, even if I don't think I did anything wrong. In the end, I think I did the right thing legally, but maybe I could have handled it more considerately to avoid making him feel wronged. So, am I the asshole? Maybe a little, because I could have been more considerate of his feelings, even if I wasn't legally in the wrong.
